requirements_summary:
Target: Redwood Private (AWS VPC) as initial deployment (EKS assumed), with future on-prem consideration.

Networking/VPC:
- VPC endpoints required for: ECR (api + dkr), S3 (gateway), STS, CloudWatch Logs, EC2, EKS, KMS, Secrets Manager, SSM (preferred), and optionally Elastic Load Balancing.
- Strong preference: no internet egress from private subnets; if unavoidable, must be explicitly controlled + allowlisted via egress proxy. They called out: "We can’t have workloads silently talking to the public internet."
- Private DNS: must work reliably (prior internal incidents w/ intermittent resolver behavior). They asked for documented resolver settings + validation steps.
- Connectivity: existing Direct Connect to AWS; they want Redwood modules to have “hooks” (outputs/placeholders) not a prescriptive DX/VPN implementation.

Logging/Audit/SIEM:
- Need VPC Flow Logs enabled by default. Destination: customer-owned S3 bucket in their logging account OR CloudWatch Logs -> subscription filter to Splunk.
- SIEM: Splunk is primary. Asked for patterns: CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to HEC / Kinesis Firehose option.
- Retention: baseline 1y for ops logs, up to 7y for certain security/audit logs (they want the retention control to be theirs).

Security/IAM:
- Customer-managed KMS keys for at-rest encryption (logs + any stateful components). Prefer key policies that restrict Redwood roles; use permission boundaries.
- Need clear list of IAM roles/policies created by Terraform modules vs expected to be pre-created by Acme.
- SSO/SAML required for Console access (later phase; not blocking the infra pilot).

Data residency:
- US-only regions. Logs must remain in US; no cross-region replication by default. Any telemetry/export out of the VPC must be explicitly opted-in.

Workload / scale assumptions (pilot):
- Phase 1 POC: internal summarization + knowledge search for ~2k users. Expected peak: 50-100 RPS for embeddings/search bursts; chat-style summarization lower concurrency but strict latency expectations.
- Latency: target p95 < 2.5s for typical summarization prompts; embeddings p95 < 300ms.

Success criteria (Acme phrasing):
- "Can deploy in our standard AWS landing zone without exceptions" (endpoints, guardrails, logging).
- Installer preflight should catch missing endpoints/private DNS issues before any long-running steps.
crm_notes:
Account: Acme Bank (enterprise). Focus is Redwood Private in AWS VPC; evaluated as a regulated banking workload w/ strict network controls.

Stage progression:
- Qualified -> Discovery (late May): initial fit confirmed (private deployment + cost controls).
- Discovery -> Demo/Eval (June): deep dive on VPC endpoints, DNS, logging, IAM boundaries; aligned on alpha Terraform modules as the path to de-risk networking.
- Eval -> Procurement (early July): Acme initiated MSA/DPA + security questionnaire; wants written security posture statements + reference architecture and rollback plan.

Key call notes (6/12 deep dive):
- Acme asked for an explicit endpoint list and why each is needed (ECR/S3/STS/CloudWatch Logs were flagged as "non-negotiable").
- They have a hard policy against unmanaged public egress. NAT gateways are acceptable only if forced and with strict egress controls; otherwise prefer VPC endpoints + private connectivity.
- SIEM integration is a gating item: must be able to export logs to Splunk. They want defaults that enable Flow Logs but keep the destination customer-owned.
- Data residency: US-only. Also asked about "where do diagnostic logs go" during install/upgrade.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm exact endpoint/DNS behavior expected by installer for image pulls (ECR + private DNS) and publish as a prerequisite checklist.
- Provide sample tfvars for a bank-style landing zone (separate logging account, centralized KMS, no public subnets if possible).
- Provide alpha upgrade guidance: pin module versions; what changes require change window (NAT/subnets/endpoints).

Internal notes:
- This account directly motivated clearer installer preflight checks around missing ECR endpoints/private DNS (see SUP-28411). Also flagged intermittent DNS behavior in private subnets (see SUP-28458).
- Acme’s security team will review IAM permission boundary approach closely; use the Security Engineering-approved templates and avoid broad wildcard actions in customer-facing examples.

Primary Redwood contacts:
- Owner/field lead: Markus Klein
- SE: Colin O'Donnell
- Product/Private: Vivek Kulkarni (as needed for alpha commitments)
- Security review: Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin (as needed for audit logging + IAM boundary posture)

Deal risk:
- Procurement cycle risk is moderate-high due to security requirements + logging retention. They will stall if we can’t give a crisp, auditable story for (1) no public egress by default, (2) customer-owned log destinations + retention controls, (3) US-only data/log residency.
